editorial:
You are dropped into the sleepy town of Centerville, where police officers Cliff and Ronnie notice strange things after polar fracking shifts the earth. Soon, the dead start walking, and the town's oddball residents must deal with a slow, messy zombie outbreak. The movie has a dry, laid-back vibe, with deadpan jokes and a cast that leans into the weirdness instead of rushing into big scares or loud action.

Bill Murray and Adam Driver are fun to watch, and Tilda Swinton steals scenes as a sword-swinging mortician. The pacing is slow and the humor is very dry, so it may not work if you want fast action or big laughs. Still, the strange tone and strong cast make it a fun late-night watch. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you want the best picture for a relaxed movie night.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the zombie outbreak fully takes over Centerville. Cliff and Ronnie try to fight back, but Ronnie already knows things will end badly because he has read the script. The town is overrun, key characters are lost or turned, and the police cannot stop the chaos. Hermit Bob watches from the woods as the quiet town falls apart, leaving the story on a bleak, deadpan note.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dry comedy and oddball zombie movies.
